feed.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
feed.subtitle: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

entry.title: Obama campaigns in Georgia as final competitive midterms map takes shape
entry.summary: With just days until Election Day, former President Barack Obama hit the campaign trail in Georgia as President Trump held a rally in Ohio and ad spending hit a record high.

entry.title: David Wasserman discusses the state of the midterms as Election Day approaches
entry.summary: NPR's A Martínez asks David Wasserman of the Cook Political Report for his take on the state of the midterms with less than a week to go until Election Day.

entry.title: Cybersecurity experts are using AI to help secure election infrastructure
entry.summary: Cybersecurity experts used AI to find a bug in a logistics system used by an independent election information agency.

entry.title: Their colleges closed, but the government refuses to erase their debts, lawsuit says
entry.summary: Federal law requires the Education Department to erase the student loans of borrowers whose colleges close suddenly. A new lawsuit claims the department isn't fully following those rules.

entry.title: The life and legacy of activist Dolores Huerta
entry.summary: NPR's A Martinez speaks with Los Angeles Times correspondent Gustavo Arellano to talk about the legacy of the late activist Dolores Huerta.

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: Trump and Obama campaign at rallies ahead of Election Day, two reports will give latest insights on GDP and inflation ahead of midterms, Israel's election is deadlocked.

entry.title: Milwaukee Brewers win their first World Series
entry.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers have won the World Series, defeating the Tampa Bay Rays in five games. It's the franchise's first-ever championship since it started more than five decades ago.

entry.title: Birth rates and immigration policies are causing an enrollment crisis for schools
entry.summary: Hundreds of thousands fewer children are born each year in the U.S. and now fewer foreign migrants live in the U.S.. Those two trends have triggered an enrollment crisis in public schools.

entry.title: Bots outnumber humans online. What does it mean for the future of the internet?
entry.summary: Bots now outnumber people online, with consequences for the economics of the internet. How does it change the way users access and pay for all the stuff done online?

entry.title: For voters from immigrant families, the needs of others is a priority at the polls
entry.summary: For young voters from immigrant families, the political calculation of voting goes beyond their individual views and includes the needs of their families and communities.
